贝尔纳·布菲 Bernard Buffet｜La Baule 拉博勒海岸 1979年原版彩色石版展览海报 法国战后具象表现主义大师布菲经典海岸题材，由传奇版画工坊Mourlot莫尔洛印制，原作是海滨版画展的官方展览海报，版内刻印艺术家签名。 这幅作品的艺术特色 1. 标志性的轮廓线条 粗重、干脆锐利的黑色轮廓线是布菲最鲜明的标签。画面里沙滩、建筑、帆船全部被硬朗黑线框定，海面、天空使用大量斜向交叉排线，自带速写的手绘张力；线条并非柔和描摹，带着棱角与速度感，扁平化处理空间，抛弃传统透视的明暗阴影，是典型布菲式平面构图语言。 ​ 2. 色彩搭配明快克制 石版画平涂高饱和度色块：澄澈的宝蓝海面、暖金黄色沙滩、翠绿色沿岸植被，色彩分区干净利落。鲜亮色块和粗黑轮廓形成强烈对比，虽然色彩活泼，却没有多余渐变混色，是石版画平印工艺带来的装饰感，非常有海报的视觉冲击力。70年代布菲的海岸系列，一改早年暗沉悲凉的基调，用明快色彩描绘法国大西洋度假海岸的休闲风光。 ​ 3. 构图的叙事与视角 采用俯瞰视角，沿着弧形绵长海滩铺开画面，弯曲的海岸线引导视线向海面延伸，错落分布的白帆形成灵动的节奏。沙滩上的躺椅、游乐设施、沿岸楼宇，简练概括地还原了拉博勒海滨度假胜地的面貌，热闹却不杂乱，把度假海岸松弛明媚的氛围浓缩在画面之中。 ​ 4. 工艺属性 莫尔洛工坊出品彩色石版画海报（Lithographic poster），石板叠色印刷，版内刻印签名，是当年展览宣传原作，区别于后期复刻印刷，在日本、欧洲中古版画流通市场认可度很高。 布菲早年作品基调沉郁，70年代海岸系列是他风格里少见的明亮题材，线条张力与清新海景融合，辨识度极高。适配新西式古典、奶油风、度假风、胡桃木轻奢空间，装饰感强，也是20世纪法国原版版画收藏热门品类。 尺寸：71.5×90.5cm，原画框，包邮

The cosmic synth pop of On All Fours marked a dramatic change from their self-titled debut albums witchy brew of punk and country; in turn, the earthy experiments of Below the Waste feel only distantly related to their previous work. On their first album, the trio of Lottie Pendlebury, Rosy Jones, and Holly Mullineaux opts for a sound thats half rustic and half avant-garde, combining electronics and grungy guitars with banjo, flute, choral vocals, and a braying violin on tracks such as "Jump Sludge." Prior to recording Below the Waste, Pendlebury listened to a lot of Deerhoof and Philip Glass; the formers influence can be felt on "Ride Around"s startling shifts, stops, and starts, while the latter informs the rippling repetition of "Perhaps" and "Sleep Talk"s woozy symphonic sweep. The way "Wheres Ur Heart"s seething atmosphere flows into "Tonight"s whispers makes for a satisfying musical arc, and the albums more considered songs are among the bands finest. "Words Fell Out" brings all of Below the Wastes elements together in a gorgeous lament; "Take It Away" lets its simple, hymnal melody build into a wave of pure emotion; and "Motorway" is a shining example of how easy the band makes ambitious, affecting pop seem. ~ Heather Phares Goat Girl are never afraid to try new things. Prior to recording Below the Waste, Pendlebury listened to a lot of Deerhoof and Philip Glass; the formers influence can be felt on "Ride Around"s startling shifts, stops, and starts, while the latter informs the rippling repetition of "Perhaps" and "Sleep Talk"s woozy symphonic sweep. Its not surprising, then, that Below the Waste is more overtly challenging listening than either of Goat Girls previous albums. Sometimes, this is an asset: the way "Wheres Ur Heart"s seething atmosphere flows into "Tonight"s whispers makes for a satisfying musical arc. Moments like the feral outburst "Tcnc," however, dilute the impact of the albums more considered songs, some of which are among the bands finest. "Words Fell Out" brings all of Below the Wastes elements together in a gorgeous lament; "Take It Away" lets its simple, hymnal melody build into a wave of pure emotion; and "Motorway" is a shining example of how easy the band makes ambitious, affecting pop seem.
